beats.text: Printed before the result was clear.
beats.note: The Chicago Tribune, 3 November 1948, the morning after the US presidential election. The first edition went to press while only early returns were in.
Printers were on strike, so the first edition had to be finished hours earlier than usual, according to the Library of Congress and WBEZ.
The paper's political correspondent assured the editor that Dewey was in, and the editor ordered the presses to roll.

beats.context: Over 150,000 copies were already on the street when the Tribune had second thoughts. Trucks were sent out to collect them.

beats.text: Truman won by more than two million votes.
beats.note: The popular vote was 24,105,812 to 21,970,065, according to the Library of Congress.

beats.name: Harry S. Truman
beats.role: On his way back to Washington, he was handed a copy and held it up for the photographers, grinning broadly.

beats.text: The deadline was real. The certainty was not.
